description: Choose pictures that help tell your idea. Learn to crop and resize them. Use pictures with care and give credit when needed.

concepts.conceptName: Choose a Picture for Its Job
questionVariants: What should you ask before adding a picture?
How can you decide if an image belongs on your page?
What question helps you choose a useful visual?
answerVariants: What will this help the reader understand?
How will this help explain my idea?
What part of my message will this help show?

concepts.conceptName: An Image Made with a Camera
questionVariants: What is a photo?
How is a photograph made?
What makes a picture a photo?
answerVariants: It is an image made with a camera.
A camera captures the image.
It comes from taking a picture with a camera.

questionVariants: What is a graphic?
What kind of visual is called a graphic?
What does the word graphic mean here?
answerVariants: A created visual, such as a drawing or sticker.
A designed picture, such as a drawing or decoration.
An image made as a design, like a drawing.

concepts.conceptName: A Small Mark with a Meaning
questionVariants: What is the job of an icon?
How does an icon help on a page?
Why use a small icon beside a label?
answerVariants: It stands for an idea, thing, or action.
It shows a meaning with a small, clear symbol.
It uses a simple symbol to represent something.

questionVariants: When might a diagram work better than a photo?
What job can a diagram do well?
Why choose a diagram to explain how something works?
answerVariants: It can make parts, steps, or links easy to see.
It shows parts or steps in a clear way.
It can explain how parts or steps connect.

concepts.conceptName: Keep Decoration in a Small Role
questionVariants: What job should decorative elements have?
How should stickers that only add style fit into a page?
How should you use images that add feeling but no facts?
answerVariants: They can add style without taking over the message.
They should support the mood and stay in a small role.
They may add feeling, but the main idea must come first.

concepts.conceptName: Hide Outer Parts of an Image
questionVariants: What does cropping do to a picture?
What changes when you crop an image?
How does a crop change what we see?
answerVariants: It hides outer parts and keeps a chosen area in view.
It removes edges from view to show a smaller area.
It shows just the chosen part by hiding the outside.

questionVariants: What should you check before cutting people out of a group photo?
A crop hides part of an event. What must you check?
What should you ask if a crop removes useful context?
answerVariants: Does it still tell the truth about what happened?
Will people still understand the event correctly?
Does the part left in view still give a true meaning?

concepts.conceptName: The Link Between Width and Height
questionVariants: What does aspect ratio compare?
Which two measurements form an image's aspect ratio?
What does aspect ratio tell about a picture's shape?
answerVariants: How wide it is compared with how tall it is.
The relationship of its width to its height.
Its width compared with its height.

questionVariants: What does it mean to distort a picture?
What happens when an image is distorted?
How can pulling just one side distort a face?
answerVariants: It is stretched or squeezed out of its normal shape.
Its shapes become too wide or too tall.
It is changed so its shapes no longer look right.

questionVariants: How can you change an image's size without squashing it?
What is a good way to resize a photo and keep its shape?
Which resizing method helps a face keep its normal shape?
answerVariants: Use a corner or the tool that keeps the proportions.
Resize with controls that keep width and height in step.
Use the corner or a setting that keeps the same proportions.

questionVariants: What is a frame in Canva?
What does a picture frame element do?
How does a frame hold an image?
answerVariants: It holds and crops a picture inside a set shape.
It keeps a picture within a chosen area or shape.
It is a shaped container that holds and crops a picture.

questionVariants: A frame hides the owl's head. What should you change?
How can you fix a photo placed too far to one side in a frame?
The crop cuts off the main subject. What can you do?
answerVariants: Move the picture inside the frame to show the subject.
Adjust the picture's position until the main part is visible.
Reposition it in the crop so the key part is in view.

questionVariants: How can you improve a search that gives too many animal pictures?
What kind of search words help find the exact owl picture you need?
How can you narrow a picture search in the class media library?
answerVariants: Name the subject and add details, such as snowy owl flying.
Use a clear subject plus details about what it is doing.
Add specific details about the subject and action.

questionVariants: What should you check if a picture looks blocky?
How can you fix a fuzzy image on your finished page?
What helps when a photo breaks into blurry squares?
answerVariants: Try a clearer image or show it at a smaller size.
Choose a sharper picture or make this one smaller.
Use a better-quality picture or reduce its size.

concepts.conceptName: Put Words on a Quiet Area
questionVariants: Words are hard to see on a busy photo. What can help?
How can you fix text placed over a jumble of picture details?
What can help words stand out when the photo behind them is busy?
answerVariants: Move them to open space or add a solid area behind them.
Use a plain area of the photo or a solid text box.
Place them on a quiet area or on a plain solid box.

questionVariants: What does copyright protect?
What kind of work has copyright protection?
What does copyright cover in this chapter?
answerVariants: Original work people create, such as art and photos.
Creative work, like drawings, photos, and illustrations.
People's original creative work.

questionVariants: What does an image license tell you?
What can you learn from a picture's license?
What does a license explain about an image?
answerVariants: How you are allowed to use it.
What uses its owner permits.
The rules for using that work.

questionVariants: What does attribution mean?
How do you give attribution for a picture?
What are you doing when you add attribution?
answerVariants: Giving credit to the person or source that made it.
Naming the creator or source to give credit.
Saying who made the work or where it came from.

questionVariants: Does finding a photo online mean you may copy it?
Can you use any picture that appears in a web search?
Does a search result give you the right to use its image?
answerVariants: No. You must check whether that use is allowed.
No. Being able to see it does not give you permission.
No. The owner's rules still apply.

questionVariants: Which picture sources should you use for class work?
Where should you look for media for a school project?
What is a safe class rule for choosing an image source?
answerVariants: Use sources your teacher has approved.
Choose the media library or sources your teacher allows.
Stay with teacher-approved places for pictures.

concepts.conceptName: Ask Before Using a Classmate's Photo
questionVariants: What should you do before using a classmate's photo?
Can you post a student's face just because you took the picture?
What is the class rule before you include another student's face?
answerVariants: Follow school rules and check with your teacher first.
Use it only as school and teacher rules allow.
Check the teacher's rules before including it.

questionVariants: Why keep notes about where an image came from?
How do image source records help later?
Why save a picture's source and use rules?
answerVariants: You can check its use rules and add credit when needed.
They help you follow permissions and keep the right credit.
You can find its permissions and creator information again.
